rv.q: The set blinks like a pinball machine, it churns out good smutty puns, but it’s oh so thin on plot, monotone on performance and even the newly penned songs by Dolly are blandly forgettable. Two Parton classics appear though, one warning us ‘too much make-up, too much hair, don’t be fooled by thinkin’ that the goods are not all there’.

“This pantomimey adaptation, sticks close to the script of the hit film but fails to replicate its sharp spirit...A stick-it-to-the-chauvinist revenge fantasy...The revenge plot is farcical, and as such it stretches itself happily into a series of upbeat but mostly forgettable musical numbers...

“This musical version swamps its story in inch-thick makeup and foot-high hair. This is very much of the more is more school of musical theatre...There’s an aimlessness and playing-for-time quality to some of these tunes that hollow it out, though there’s still a lot of fun...

“Parton's somewhat hallucinatory musical is a wilfully preposterous crowd-pleaser...Although this show started out...in 2005, it feels pretty post-Weinstein, with its uncompromising focus on male shitness and violent retribution...The plot is about as ridiculous as these women’s ultra-glam interpretation of ‘office wear’...

Without a shadow of a doubt though, the best of the three is Davies. There was a very mixed response when the Love Island star was announced to be taking on the role of Judy, many questioning her ability and suggesting it was merely a marketing scheme (casting a ‘name’ to help sell the show), which sadly seems to be far too common in modern theatre.
